question: Oxidation in oxy-acetylene welding can lead to _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __Porosity and oxide defects**(Option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Oxidation in oxy-acetylene welding__ can lead to porosity and oxide defects in the weld.
 
• Porosity refers to the formation of voids or cavities, which can weaken the weld.
 
• Oxide defects occur when excessive oxidation prevents the proper fusion of metal surfaces.
 
• To avoid oxidation, proper welding techniques and settings must be maintained, including the correct balance of oxygen and acetylene.
 
• Oxidation can compromise weld integrity and reduce durability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Welding Techniques:**
 
 
• Proper adjustment of the flame is crucial to prevent oxidation and ensure a high-quality weld.
 
• Using flux can help reduce oxidation by shielding the molten metal from air.
 
 
 
• **Types of Defects:**
 
 
• Other common welding defects include cracks, incomplete fusion, and undercut.
 
• These defects can compromise the strength and appearance of the weld.
 
 
 
• **Welding Safety:**
 
 
• Proper safety equipment, such as gloves and goggles, should be used to protect against hazards.
 
• Ensure adequate ventilation when welding in enclosed spaces to avoid harmful fume exposure.
